learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn how to build complete, meaningful sentences and easily identify the four main types we use to express ourselves every day!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense when put together. It always starts with a capital letter, contains a subject and a verb, and ends with proper punctuation!
These sentences simply tell us something or give us information, like 'The sun rises in the east.' They are the most common type of sentence and always end with a full stop.
Whenever you are curious and want to know something, you use an interrogative sentence! They always ask a question and must end with a question mark.
We use imperative sentences to give orders, offer advice, or make a polite request, like 'Please close the door.' They usually end with a full stop, and the subject 'you' is often hidden!
Wow! When you want to show sudden surprise, joy, anger, or excitement, you use an exclamatory sentence. They always end with an exclamation mark to show that burst of emotion.

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Room Detective Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Look around your room right now and write down four sentences: one fact about it, one question you have, one command to clean it, and one big surprise you see!

quick_recap: ⭐ A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense.
⭐ Declarative sentences share facts and end with a full stop (.).
⭐ Interrogative sentences ask questions and end with a question mark (?).
⭐ Imperative sentences give commands or requests and usually end with a full stop (.).
⭐ Exclamatory sentences show strong feelings and end with an exclamation mark (!).
